sentiment.rationale: The document reports enormous revenue growth (up 54% YoY) and a raised full-year guidance ($2B lift at midpoint), but also discloses a 15% decline in US realized prices and a 27% increase in R&D expenses, raising durability concerns. The worksheet's own rationale states 'a beat-and-raise may already be in a stock trading at a steep premium' and that 'falling US pricing and heavy reinvestment are the details that get sold even on a raise,' leading to a negative sentiment score.

summary.revenue: Revenue up 54% year over year, with key product sales of $12B in the quarter.
summary.eps: Non-GAAP EPS $7.02 against $1.18 a year earlier.
summary.guidance: Full-year revenue guidance raised to $63.0B to $63.5B, a $2B lift at the midpoint. Non-GAAP EPS range lifted to $23.23 to $23.70.
key_risks: US realized prices fell 15% in the quarter.
The CVS formulary switch created patient and physician disruption, though the Zepbound impact was called modest.
International obesity reimbursement remains thin, so uptake leans on out-of-pocket payers.
key_opportunities: Zepbound US prescriptions tripled year over year, taking 71% of new starts.
Lilly gained market share in the incretin analogs market for the fifth consecutive quarter.
Orforglipron filings on track for year end.
